purpose: Externally testable asset for Fortune-500 auditor / CereVasc acquisition evaluation

invention_definition.title: Controlled retention of a CNS therapeutic in the CSF compartment while maintaining clinically adequate CSF drainage through an endovascular CSF-to-venous shunt
invention_definition.mechanism: Size-selective retention element permits CSF passage while retaining therapeutic molecules above a molecular weight threshold. CSF drainage continues through the shunt. Therapeutic exposure increases because the drug is not immediately cleared by drainage.

A_retention_while_draining.claim: A method of controlling therapeutic exposure in the CSF of a patient via an endovascular CSF-to-venous shunt, comprising: delivering a therapeutic agent into the CSF via the shunt; selectively retaining said agent via a size-selective element that permits CSF passage while retaining molecules above a threshold; maintaining clinically adequate CSF drainage through said shunt; wherein therapeutic exposure is increased relative to unretained delivery while drainage is preserved.
A_retention_while_draining.design_around_risk: MEDIUM — retention mechanisms exist in other contexts but not in eShunt
A_retention_while_draining.eShunt_specific: PARTIALLY — works in any shunt, but venous boundary (L6) adds eShunt specificity

B_retention_plus_separation.claim: The method of claim A, further comprising: delivering said agent at a location separated from the dominant CSF drainage path, wherein the combination of separation and retention creates controlled therapeutic residence.
B_retention_plus_separation.novelty: L3 (separation) is NOT novel (found in 2 CereVasc patents). L4 is novel. Combination untested.

C_retention_plus_adaptive.claim: The method of claim A, further comprising: estimating CSF drug concentration from hydraulic state and dosing history; adjusting drug delivery based on said estimate; maintaining CSF drainage throughout.
C_retention_plus_adaptive.novelty: UNKNOWN — needs separate hostile analysis. Not assumed patentable.
C_retention_plus_adaptive.note: C connects Position #1 (hydraulic state estimation) with Position #3 (drug delivery). Potential platform invention. Needs its own search later.

simulation_evidence.primary_result: 288% median model-derived relative tissue exposure improvement (retention-only vs CereVasc baseline)
simulation_evidence.classification: MODEL_DERIVED PK RELATIVE EXPOSURE — not clinical benefit, not therapeutic efficacy
simulation_evidence.robustness: 8/8 model formulations survived; N=500 Monte Carlo (100% >20%); N=100 platform test (100% >20%); 7/7 adversarial scenarios survived; 5-compartment model with realistic CNS transport

CereVasc_baseline.interpretation: CereVasc's existing delivery — no retention, no separation

separation_alone.interpretation: Secondary — separation also works but is NOT novel (L3 found in prior art)

3x_dose_baseline.interpretation: Architecture (288%) beats dose escalation (200%) — more value than simply increasing dose

controlled_release_alone.interpretation: USELESS without retention — drug is still cleared by drainage. Retention is essential.

standard_intrathecal.interpretation: Standard IT (no eShunt drainage) is better than CereVasc baseline but worse than retention architecture

simulation_evidence.causal_mechanism: SELECTIVE RETENTION is the primary cause (288% alone). Architecture beats 3x dose (200%). Release alone is useless (2%).

103.motivation_note: No motivation evidence found in searched corpus. But 'NONE FOUND' is too strong because the search is incomplete. The correct state is SEARCH_INCOMPLETE: we searched what we could and found nothing, but we cannot claim nothing exists.

distinction_enforced.nothing_found: We searched 15 patents + PatSnap queries and found no motivation to combine retention + drainage in eShunt context.
distinction_enforced.nothing_exists: We CANNOT claim nothing exists — the search is PARTIAL. EPO OPS, USPTO ODP, Lens.org are not configured.
distinction_enforced.rule: The machine must distinguish 'nothing found in searched corpus' from 'nothing exists in the world'. The former is SUPPORTED. The latter is NOT SUPPORTED.

103.103_status: UNCERTAIN — leans NON_OBVIOUS (HYPOTHESIS, not legal conclusion). Patent counsel opinion required.
103.critical_rule: Do NOT say 'NONE FOUND' when the search is incomplete. Say 'SEARCH_INCOMPLETE — no motivation found in searched corpus, but search is not complete.'

model_result.rationale: The safety model shows drainage preserved at all fouling levels (0-100%) with bypass activation. However, this is MODEL_DERIVED. The physical experiment must test the bypass mechanism separately.

physical_test_required.test: Fouling simulation — intentionally occlude retention element and verify bypass activates
physical_test_required.measurement: CSF flow, ICP, bypass state during induced occlusion
physical_test_required.safety_threshold: ICP < 20 mmHg during induced occlusion; drainage >= 0.3 mL/min via bypass
physical_test_required.in_experiment: Add 2 additional animals in Group B for fouling safety test (induced occlusion at 24h)

model_result.buyer_condition: Therapeutic retention must never compromise the primary hydrocephalus-drainage function. MODEL: PASS. PHYSICAL: NOT YET TESTED.

safety.buyer_condition: Therapeutic retention must never compromise drainage. MODEL: PASS. PHYSICAL: NOT YET TESTED.

experiment_protocol.title: Selective retention of CNS therapeutic in CSF while maintaining drainage: ovine pharmacokinetic comparison
experiment_protocol.primary_question: Does selective retention produce a material increase in target-tissue exposure over CereVasc's existing delivery architecture, without compromising CSF drainage or ICP safety?
experiment_protocol.hypothesis: Group B (retention-only) tissue AUC >= 150% of Group A (CereVasc baseline). Model predicts 288%.

A_baseline.description: CereVasc existing delivery (endovascular, no retention, US11850390B2 architecture)

B_retention.description: Retention-only architecture (size-selective membrane, no spatial separation)

design.blinding: Outcome assessor blinded (laboratory personnel measuring fluorescence unaware of group assignment). Surgeon cannot be blinded (device visible).
design.agent: FITC-dextran 150 kDa (surrogate for bevacizumab, matching MW)

sampling_schedule.tissue: post-mortem at 48h (brain, cervical cord, lumbar cord)

primary.name: Target-tissue AUC
primary.power: 80% (based on effect size d=1.014, n=8 per group)

secondary.name: CSF AUC
secondary.measurement: CSF concentration × time from serial sampling

secondary.name: Systemic/venous exposure
secondary.measurement: Venous blood drug concentration — systemic loss

secondary.name: Bypass activation
secondary.measurement: Whether bypass valve activated during study
secondary.safety_test: Bypass must activate if ICP > threshold

effect_thresholds.success: Group B tissue AUC >= 150% of Group A (p < 0.05, one-sided)
effect_thresholds.milestone: Group B tissue AUC >= 120% of Group A (improvement confirmed, magnitude smaller than model)
effect_thresholds.failure: Group B tissue AUC <= 100% of Group A (no improvement)
effect_thresholds.safety_failure: ICP > 20 mmHg OR drainage < 0.3 mL/min in either group

analysis_plan.primary: Wilcoxon rank-sum test (one-sided, alpha=0.05). Report median, IQR, and 95% CI for ratio B/A.
analysis_plan.secondary: Descriptive statistics for all secondary endpoints. No multiplicity adjustment (exploratory).
analysis_plan.safety: Continuous monitoring. If any animal has ICP > 20 mmHg for > 5 minutes, record as safety event.
analysis_plan.missing_data: If animal dies before 48h, use available data up to death. Report as protocol deviation.
analysis_plan.interim_analysis: None (small sample, not powered for interim).

sample_size_justification.rationale: Based on conservative effect size d=1.014 (ln(1.5)/0.4), n=8 per group provides 80% power at alpha=0.05 (one-sided). Model predicts 288% (d>>1), so 150% threshold is very conservative.

decision_tree.AUC_B >= 200% AND safety: BUYABLE CONFIRMED — proceed to patent filing + partnership discussions
decision_tree.AUC_B 150-200% AND safety: BUYABLE LIKELY — improvement confirmed at conservative threshold; recalibrate model; proceed with caution
decision_tree.AUC_B 120-150% AND safety: MILESTONE-WORTHY — direction correct, magnitude smaller; recalibrate and reassess buyer value
decision_tree.AUC_B <= 120%: TRUE CEILING — model overestimated in vivo; territory needs new mechanism hypothesis
decision_tree.Safety failure: ARCHITECTURE FAILED — retention compromises drainage; redesign required

experiment_protocol.timeline: 12 weeks (4 weeks setup, 4 weeks in-life, 4 weeks analysis)
experiment_protocol.commercial_context: CereVasc has demonstrated ovine CNS biodistribution via eShunt (scAAV9). This experiment directly compares against their EXISTING delivery method — the most commercially meaningful comparison possible.
experiment_protocol.pre_registration_statement: This protocol is pre-registered BEFORE any experimental data exists. The hash 5bfaec842f932243 is stored to prevent post-hoc modification of endpoints or thresholds.

buyer_utility.value_proposition: Increase the value of every future CNS therapy delivered through eShunt by controlling exposure rather than merely providing access.
buyer_utility.cerevasc_strategy_alignment: CereVasc publicly seeks pharma/biotech partners for CNS therapy delivery (EXTERNAL_EVIDENCE). Controlled exposure is what pharma requires.
buyer_utility.platform_advantage: Architecture benefits antibodies, oligonucleotides, gene therapy vectors, and small molecules (MODEL_DERIVED, N=100, 100% >20%)
